metadata.source: Honda 2020 EICMA release and first-generation SC82 press/owner specifications; BSD/Bennetts 2020 UK stock rear-wheel dyno
metadata.notes: European 2020 specification: 81 x 48.5 mm, compression 13.0, four 52 mm throttles, 32.5/28.5 mm valve heads, 201 kg curb mass, 1455 mm wheelbase, 120/70-17 and 200/55-17 tyres. Honda reference 160 kW at 14500 rpm and 113 Nm at 12500 rpm. Japanese release lists compression 13.2; do not mix that market into this preset. SP has standard up/down quickshifter, ABS, HSTC, Start Mode and slipper clutch; simulator interventions approximate the equipment. Cam lift 10/10 mm, 110-degree centres and 225 degrees at 0.050 inch (256.5 degrees estimated seat duration) are provisional engine-sim cbr1000.mr inputs, NOT verified stock SC82 cam measurements. Runner equivalent bore 52 mm is an ESTIMATE from butterfly size, not measured port taper. Default runner length/port volume, piston/rod/flywheel/wheel masses, slant, clutch 200 Nm crank capacity, drag area 0.35 m2, limiter 15000 rpm and shift timings are estimates. Honda's quoted Cd 0.270 is dimensionless and is NOT the drag area; no measured frontal area is available. No ECU binary or guessed US throttle restriction is used. Online reference is the UK base RR-R stock powertrain (shared with SP), 199.76 wheel hp at 13900 rpm and 78.96 lb-ft at 12500 rpm, DIN corrected, fourth gear. Estimated wheel output uses the simulator's existing 93% drivetrain efficiency. Sources: https://global.honda/en/newsroom/news/2019/2191105aeng.html ; https://hondanews.ca/en-CA/hci-power/releases/release-b6701d6c6a3ec3934c67bf479d61e09a21b3cd41-2020-honda-cbr1000rr-r-fireblade-sp ; https://global.honda/jp/news/2020/2200305-cbr1000rr-r.html ; https://www.bennetts.co.uk/bikesocial/reviews/bikes/honda/honda-cbr1000rr-r-fireblade-sp-2020-review-price-spec
